questions.q: What does the Journal Entries Report primarily organize its output by?
options: By GL account only
By transaction, batch, or period, for a given ledger and subledger application
By supplier payment terms
By employee name
questions.explain: The Journal Entries Report lists subledger journal entries scoped by ledger, application, date range, or batch — transaction-oriented, not account-oriented.

questions.q: What does the Account Analysis Report let you see that the Journal Entries Report does not emphasize?
options: A list of every supplier's bank account number
A list of every password used to log into Oracle Fusion
The ledger's functional currency
Every subledger journal line that posted to a specific GL account over a period, regardless of which transaction it came from
questions.explain: The Account Analysis Report organizes by account rather than by transaction, showing everything that hit a chosen account over a period.

questions.q: Why does the usefulness of these two reports depend directly on Chapter 2's rule-building choices?
options: It doesn't; report usefulness has nothing to do with rule configuration
Because well-built description rules and thoughtfully assigned accounting classes make report lines specific and meaningfully grouped, instead of generic and undifferentiated
Because reports can only be run if an AAD has never been modified
Because reports require a secondary ledger to function at all
questions.explain: Description rules and accounting classes, both configured in Chapter 2, directly determine how informative and well-organized these reports are.

questions.q: When would a controller most likely reach for the Account Analysis Report?
options: When reviewing an entire period's Payables activity transaction by transaction
When setting up a new Chart of Accounts segment
When configuring a new accounting method
When a specific GL account balance looks unexpected and they need to see the detail behind it
questions.explain: The Account Analysis Report is the natural tool for drilling into why a specific account's balance looks the way it does.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how might a consultant typically use both reports together during an investigation?
options: They would never use both reports in the same investigation
Only auditors are permitted to use the Account Analysis Report
Starting broad with the Journal Entries Report to spot something unusual, then narrowing to the Account Analysis Report for the specific account involved
The two reports are functionally identical and interchangeable
questions.explain: A common workflow moves from a broad, transaction-oriented report to a focused, account-oriented report once a specific account of interest is identified.
